document_title: PS22/9 – A new Consumer Duty: Feedback to CP21/36 and final rules

sections.title: 1 Summary
sections.reason: Introductory and explanatory material summarising the Duty and feedback, without standalone, checkable rules about the content or presentation of consumer communications beyond what later chapters detail.

sections.title: 2 The scope of the Duty
sections.reason: Focuses on which firms, products and relationships are in scope rather than prescribing how marketing or consumer‑facing communications must be drafted or presented.

sections.title: 3 Application to existing products and services
sections.reason: Deals with how the Duty applies over time to firms’ existing books and closed products, which cannot be audited by inspecting communication texts alone.

sections.title: 4 The Consumer Principle and disapplication of Principles 6 and 7
sections.reason: Sets the overarching Consumer Principle and how it replaces Principles 6 and 7, providing high‑level conduct standards that marketing and other consumer communications must not breach.

sections.title: 5 The cross‑cutting rules
sections.reason: Contains general rules (e.g. act in good faith, avoid foreseeable harm) that apply to all interactions including marketing, and can be tested against the content and tone of consumer communications.

sections.title: 6 The products and services outcome
sections.reason: Addresses product and service design, target markets and distribution, which largely concern internal processes and cannot be assessed from communications text alone.

sections.title: 7 The price and value outcome
sections.reason: Focuses on fair value assessments and pricing structures rather than specific, checkable requirements for how marketing or disclosures must be written or presented.

sections.title: 8 The consumer understanding outcome
sections.reason: Sets explicit rules about the clarity, timing, framing and presentation of information so that consumers understand products, which can be audited directly from marketing and communication texts.

sections.title: 9 The consumer support outcome
sections.reason: Includes requirements about how support options and processes are communicated and made accessible to consumers, some of which can be checked by reviewing customer‑facing communications and scripts.

sections.title: 10 Consumers in vulnerable circumstances
sections.reason: Imposes standards for treating vulnerable consumers fairly, including how firms communicate with them and adapt wording or channels, which can be assessed from tailored communications.

sections.title: 11 A private right of action
sections.reason: Discusses whether consumers have a private right of action under the Duty, a legal enforcement issue rather than rules about communication content or presentation.

sections.title: 12 Implementation timetable
sections.reason: Sets dates, phases and planning expectations for implementation, which concern firm project management rather than the substance of marketing communications.

sections.title: 13 Monitoring and governance
sections.reason: Covers internal governance, MI, and oversight arrangements that cannot be audited by reading external customer communications alone.

sections.title: 14 Our approach to the Consumer Duty
sections.reason: Explains the FCA’s supervisory and enforcement approach and high‑level philosophy rather than imposing specific, text‑level communication requirements.

sections.title: 15 Cost benefit analysis
sections.reason: Analyses expected costs and benefits of the Duty and does not contain operative rules or standards for marketing or consumer communications.

sections.title: Annex 1 List of non‑confidential respondents to CP21/36
sections.reason: Provides a list of consultation respondents only, with no regulatory obligations or guidance on communications.

sections.title: Annex 2 Abbreviations used in this paper
sections.reason: Contains abbreviations and definitions for reading the paper and no standalone obligations about marketing or consumer communications; the exact end of this annex and any following appendix content cannot be reliably inferred beyond the total page count.
